description: Reference implementation: call public AIDP / OCI APIs from a custom code tool using an OCI API-key signer resolved at runtime from AIDP's Credential Store. No PEM files in the zip; no hardcoded keys in source.

tools.description: Resolves an OCI signer from the Credential Store and calls the public AIDP data-plane API. Test panel needs only: op + credential_name. The credential bundle supplies the keys (tenancy/user/fingerprint/private_key) AND the connection (data_lake_ocid, region). Default op=map walks the whole Master catalog and returns every catalog/schema/table/volume/KB key.

schema.name: op
schema.description: map = one-shot: walk the whole Master catalog (catalogs -> schemas -> tables/volumes/KBs) and return every key + a readable text tree. whoami = prove the signer authenticates. The list_*/get_* ops do a single level (they read catalog_key/schema_key/volume_key/kb_key/path from conf).

schema.name: credential_name
schema.description: Display name of the SECRET_TOKEN credential (or an OCI Vault secret OCID). Bundle keys: tenancy, user, fingerprint, private_key (required) + data_lake_ocid, region (optional — supplies the connection so nothing else is needed here). Falls back to conf.credential_name.

auth.note: The agent runtime uses resource principal to call aidputils.secrets internally. The OCI signer the tool then uses is resolved per-invocation from the Credential Store — no permanent PEM in this zip.

credential_name.placeholder: Display name of the SECRET_TOKEN credential in AIDP
credential_name.help: AIDP → Settings → Credentials. Type: SECRET_TOKEN. Keys: tenancy / user / fingerprint / private_key, plus optional data_lake_ocid + region.

data_lake_ocid.help: Optional — prefer putting data_lake_ocid on the credential bundle. Used only if the bundle omits it.

catalog_key.help: Only for the single-level list_*/get_* ops. op=map ignores this unless you want to scope to one catalog.
